title: Zakariyya's silence
hookLine: his sign is three days without speaking except by gesture, and remembering Allah (3:41)
tomorrow: Maryam above the women of the worlds

lines: AN OLD MAN STARTS TO PRAY.
cards: An old man walks into a small prayer room to check on the girl he's raising. She's Maryam; he's her guardian, Zakariyya. Beside her is food he didn't bring.
Where did this come from, he asks. From God, she says; God provides for whom He wills, beyond counting.
And the old man, who has no children and a wife who never could, stands right there and starts to pray for a child of his own.

teach.h: THE MIHRAB: FOOD HE DIDN'T BRING
teach.b: That's 3:37 and 38. The prayer room is the mihrab, the same word used today for the niche in a mosque's wall that shows the direction of prayer. What Zakariyya saw there made him brave enough to ask.
Then 3:39: while he's still standing in prayer, the angels call to him with good news of a son, Yahya, who will confirm a word from God, noble, chaste, and a prophet.
And Zakariyya, who has just asked for exactly this, asks how. I'm old. My wife is barren.
The answer, in Pickthall's words: "So (it will be). Allah doeth what He will." He asks for a sign, and the sign is strange.
In 3:41 he won't speak to people for three days, except by ramz, by gesture. And: remember your Lord much, and glorify Him in the evening and the morning.
In Surah Maryam, the nineteenth, the same sign is three nights, and he comes out and signals to his people to glorify God morning and evening. Commentators differ on why it came this way.
Some read the silence as a mercy, a sign he could feel in his own body. Others note his tongue was stopped from talk with people, never from remembering God.
Christians tell a story of the same man, Zechariah, in the Gospel of Luke.
In the Qur'an's telling, the point lands on what filled the silence: no small talk, no explaining, no complaining. Only gestures, and dhikr, remembrance, morning and evening.

how: Muslims honor Zakariyya and Yahya as prophets; his story (3:37–41 and Surah Maryam) is often recited by those hoping for a child, and his sign of silence filled with remembrance is a model for quiet dhikr in the morning and evening.

o: three days with no speech, only gesture and remembrance
quiet prayer said only in the heart, never aloud
a lifelong vow never to speak to people again

p: the prayer room where Maryam was
the length of the sign in 3:41

s: Zakariyya started praying for a child after seeing Maryam's food
3:37–38: he found provision with her, then prayed for a child right there.
his three days of silence meant no prayer at all
he was told to remember his Lord much, evening and morning.
the mihrab is only a modern mosque word
the Qur'an uses it for the place where Maryam stayed and Zakariyya prayed.

games.q: you're Zakariyya. the angels have just told you you'll have a son, though you're old. you ask for a sign. what is it?
o: you won't speak to people for three days, except by gesture.
your wife will dream of the child.
games.why: three days of silence, speaking only by gesture, and remembering God much, evening and morning (3:41).

practice: Close your mouth gently and let the silence settle, noticing how much talk runs inside you even when you aren't speaking.
Each time a sentence starts to form, let it go and come back to one simple remembrance: if you pray, subhanallah, glory be to God, and if you don't, simply the breath.

wordCard.voice: Zakariyya's silence. Three days without speech, only gesture, filled with remembrance, morning and evening. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: by gesture, by sign (3:41); the only way Zakariyya spoke to people for three days.

carryVoice: Your line: silent and remembering. A silence can be full of remembrance. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: So (it will be). Allah doeth what He will.
